title: Projective-bundle formula without purity
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,r}$, $r\geq1$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $n\geq0$, and let $F$ be a locally free $\mathcal O_B$-module of constant rank $n+1$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Put $p:P=\mathbf P_B(F)=\operatorname{Proj}_B(\operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}F)\to B$, with its tautological invertible module $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry], and put $h_F=c_{1,A}(\mathcal O_P(1))$ [lem-pur-kummer-additivity]. In the ordinary pro-etale derived category of constant-$A$ modules, the adjoints of its cup powers give an isomorphism
$$(1,h_F,\ldots,h_F^n):\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}A_B(-a)[-2a]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*A_P,$$
with the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and the derived operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every $g:B'\to B$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, proper base change and the tautological pullback identification identify the pullback of this morphism with the same morphism for $g^*F$ on $B'$. This is the finite-coefficient statement; it uses no smooth or higher-codimension purity isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry], $p$ is proper, $P$ is separated finite type over $k$, and $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is a global line bundle whose restriction to every trivialization is the usual $\mathcal O(1)$. Form $h_F$ by [lem-pur-kummer-additivity]. For $a\geq0$, tensor $a$ copies of $h_F:A_P\to A_P(1)[2]$, multiply the coefficient twists, and use evaluation to view the result as $p^*A_B(-a)[-2a]\to A_P$; $a=0$ is the identity. The twists are invertible, locally free rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives the displayed component into $Rp_*A_P$; the finite direct sum gives the asserted morphism $\Phi_F$. No gluing of derived-category morphisms is used.

source.place: Step 2, global Kummer class before taking fibres

proof.text:
We may calculate the same morphism on the ordinary etale sites. The definition in [lem-pur-kummer-additivity] constructs $h_F$ by applying $
u_P^*$ to the etale Kummer morphism, with its prescribed twist identification. The counit-mate isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] identifies $
u_B^*Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}A_P$ with $Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_P$. Its displayed counit equality says that the adjunct of the image of a component is exactly the image of its adjunct, so it identifies $
u_B^*\Phi_F^{\mathrm{et}}$ with $\Phi_F$. Pullback and tensor comparisons respect these cup powers by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and finite etale twists pull back as in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The comparison functor is fully faithful by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], hence reflects isomorphisms. The compact and supported calculations below may be made in either site using the named comparisons in [lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility].

source.place: Step 1 and Step 2, finite-coefficient etale/pro-etale interpretation

proof.text:
Work over the fixed $k$. Apply [thm-pur-rank-one-thom] to the trivial line over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,A)=A(-1)[-2]$, and $\tau_E$, the compact direct image of the zero-section class precomposed with $A=R\Gamma(\{0\},A)$, is invertible; this is $u_{\{0\}}$ of [lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility], so $u_{\{0\}}(\partial\kappa(t))$ generates $H^2_c(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))$. The class is $\partial\kappa(t)$ by [lem-pur-divisor-class], with residue $1$ by [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]. [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology] gives $R\Gamma_c(\operatorname{Spec}k,A)=A$. Coefficients are twists of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$; iterating the compact isomorphism $\kappa_c$ on $\mathbf A^n_k=\mathbf A^{n-1}_k\times_k\mathbf A^1_k$ gives
$$R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^n_k,A)=A(-n)[-2n].$$
By [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] the pullback of $\partial\kappa(t)$ along the $i$th projection is $\partial\kappa(t_i)$, and pullback preserves supported cups [def-pur-supported-cup]. The cup clause of the compact lemma (degrees even) and associativity identify $\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_n)$, supported at the origin $o$, with the supported exterior product [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] of $\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_{n-1})$ and $\partial\kappa(t)$. The supports are points, hence proper, so $u_{Z\times W}\circ\kappa^{Z,W}=\kappa_c\circ(u_Z\otimes_A^Lu_W)$ and invertibility of $\kappa_c$ between free rank-one modules show by induction on $n$ that $u_o(\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_n))$ generates $H^{2n}_c(\mathbf A^n_k,A(n))$, not merely that the group is free of rank one. All shifts are even.

source.place: Step 1, compact affine-space calculation and normalization

proof.text: Set up induction on $n$ for $\Phi_n$ on $\mathbf P^n_k$. At $n=0$ this is the identity. For $n\geq1$, write $H=\{T_0=0\}\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$, $U=\{T_0\ne0\}\cong\mathbf A^n_k$, and $o=[1:0:\cdots:0]$, using [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]. The $n$ divisors $D_i=\{T_i=0\}$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ have common intersection $o$ and $\mathcal O(D_i)=\mathcal O(1)$. By [lem-pur-divisor-class], forgetting support sends each localized class to $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Form their supported cup product as in [def-pur-supported-cup]. Its restriction to $U$ is the coordinate product from step 3, by [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] and the local-equation description of the divisor class. Excision and the support-to-compact comparison of [lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility] identify its image in $H^{2n}(\mathbf P^n_k,A(n))$ with the image of that compactly supported coordinate product. Forgetting support in the tensor-morphism definition multiplies the underlying ordinary classes, so this image is exactly $h^n$. In particular the compact generator maps to $h^n$.

source.place: Step 1, coordinate hyperplanes and the top class

proof.text:
Apply the actual open--closed triangle of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] to $U\subset\mathbf P^n_k$ and the constant complex, then proper direct image to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is
$$R\Gamma_c(U,A)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\mathbf P^n_k,A)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(H,A)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(U,A)[1].$$
Here $R\Gamma(\mathbf P^n_k,j_!A)=R\Gamma_c(U,A)$ for the compactification $U\subset\mathbf P^n_k$ by [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The first term is concentrated in degree $2n$ by step 3. The induction hypothesis puts the last term in even degrees $0,2,\ldots,2n-2$. The long exact cohomology sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] therefore identifies restriction with an isomorphism in every degree below $2n$, and identifies $H_c^{2n}(U,A)$ with $H^{2n}(\mathbf P^n_k,A)$; all other groups vanish. Naturality of $c_1$ in [lem-pur-kummer-additivity] gives $h|_H=c_1(\mathcal O_H(1))$, so $1,h,\ldots,h^{n-1}$ are the required generators in the lower degrees. Step 4 gives $h^n$ as the top generator. Consequently $\Phi_n$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf and hence its pro-etale realization is an isomorphism by clause 3 of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], using the point sections/stalk identification of step 3. Full faithfulness from step 2 makes the etale morphism an isomorphism as well; cohomology is [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. This proves the induction without a claimed splitting of a triangle or a purity isomorphism.

For arbitrary geometric fields use the same Kummer construction without imposing finite type over $k$ on the extension. For any scheme map $v:T'\to T$, pullback of a line bundle takes its frame torsor to the extension of its inverse-image torsor along the units comparison (on transition functions this is just $g_{ij}\mapsto v^*g_{ij}$); the torsor--$H^1$ bijection is functorial by [lem-sc-etale-torsor-h1-functoriality]. The unit-pullback map gives a morphism from the inverse-image Kummer sequence to the Kummer sequence on $T'$ [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Naturality of connecting maps in [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback], followed by $z\mapsto z\otimes1$, proves $v^*c_1(M)=c_1(v^*M)$. Twist evaluation commutes with this by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. These are three applications of the cited statements, so the calculation also applies to $T'=\mathbf P^n_\Omega$ for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. Now [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry] identifies $\mathbf P^n_\Omega$ and its $\mathcal O(1)$ with the base changes from $k$. Ordinary etale proper base change [prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change] for $\mathbf P^n_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ identifies the pullback of $\Phi_n^{\mathrm{et}}$ with the same cup-power morphism over $\Omega$, hence with an isomorphism. Here [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] supplies the A-linear exchange and says its invertibility is detected by the underlying abelian exchange. The rank-one and Kunneth theorems themselves were used only over $k$.

For the given $B$, use $\Phi_F^{\mathrm{et}}$ from step 2. At a geometric point $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$, proper base change [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] identifies its target stalk with $R\Gamma(P_{\bar b},A)$. The geometric fibre is $\mathbf P^n_\Omega$, with the tautological $\mathcal O(1)$, by [lem-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-geometry]. The Kummer construction [lem-pur-kummer-additivity], with its arbitrary-scheme pullback calculation of step 6, identifies the stalk map with the map proved invertible in step 6. Its source and target are bounded-below etale module complexes. Clause 3 of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] therefore makes $\nu_B^*\Phi_F^{\mathrm{et}}$ an isomorphism, identified with $\Phi_F$ by step 2. The detector is explicitly restricted to etale-origin morphisms; no geometric-stalk assertion for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves is used.

Finally let $g:B'\to B$ be as in the statement. The geometry lemma identifies $P'=B'\times_BP$ and $\mathcal O_{P'}(1)=g'^*\mathcal O_P(1)$. By [lem-pur-kummer-additivity] and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], the adjunct of the $a$th pulled-back etale component is $g'^*h_F^a=h_{g^*F}^a$ after evaluation of opposite twists. The A-module exchange of clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] is defined by pulling back the counit and transposing; thus composing the pulled-back component with exchange has precisely this adjunct, and adjunction identifies it with the $a$th component of $\Phi_{g^*F}^{\mathrm{et}}$. This proves equality of the maps, including $a=0$, and not just fibrewise isomorphy. Proper base change [prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change] makes exchange invertible. Pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the counit equality of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] carry that same equality to pro-etale coefficients. This proves the stated base-change compatibility.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $F$ be a
vector bundle of rank
$n+1$ on $B$, let $p:\mathbf P_B(F)\to B$, and put
$h_F=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ of [lem-pur-kummer-additivity].
Then the morphism

$$
(1,h_F,\ldots,h_F^n):
\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\Lambda_B(-a)[-2a]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf P_B(F)}
$$

is an isomorphism, base-change compatible.

proof.text:
The vanishing of a bounded cone will be checked on its cohomology sheaves in the sense of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].
Step 1: the field case. Let the base be an algebraically closed
field and write $H=\mathbf P^{n-1}$ for the hyperplane at infinity
of $\mathbf P^n$, with complement $\mathbf A^n$. By
[thm-pur-rank-one-thom] on the fiber-wise structure, the Künneth
formula for compactly supported cohomology
[cor-kun-compact-kunneth] of the Künneth chapter — the
*compact-support* statement, which is not the closed-support Künneth
[lem-pur-kunneth-supported]: cohomology with support in the whole space
is ordinary cohomology, whereas $R\Gamma_c$ is computed on a
compactification — and induction,

$$
R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^n,\Lambda)\;\cong\;\Lambda(-n)[-2n].
$$

Apply the open–closed localization triangle of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement] to
$\mathbf A^n\subset\mathbf P^n$. By induction on $n$,
restriction to $H$ identifies $1,h,\ldots,h^{n-1}$ with the
corresponding basis of $R\Gamma(H,\Lambda)$, and the remaining class
$h^n$ restricts to zero on $H$. Choose $n$ hyperplanes whose
intersection is the origin of the affine chart; the product of their
localized Kummer classes is supported at the origin, and after
forgetting support and extending to $\mathbf P^n$ it is
$h^n$; under the Künneth isomorphism this supported product is the
generator of
$R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^n,\Lambda)=\Lambda(-n)[-2n]$ fixed by the
rank-one normalization ([thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]).
Therefore

$$
\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n}\Lambda(-a)[-2a]
\xrightarrow{\ (1,h,\ldots,h^n)\ }R\Gamma(\mathbf P^n,\Lambda)
$$

is an isomorphism.

Step 2: the general base. The Kummer class $h_F$ is global; the
class of the divisors in Step 1 is the one of
[lem-pur-divisor-class] (the frame class of the
$\mathbf P^n$-bundle, with the independence of
[lem-pur-frame-independence]), so the morphism of the statement
is defined before taking any fiber. Proper base change
([prop-weil-proet-finite-proper-base-change]) with
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] identifies its pullback to
each geometric point of $B$ with the calculation of Step 1; the
cone is bounded constructible with zero geometric stalks, hence zero.
The same argument for the pullbacks proves base-change compatibility.
This proof used only the rank-one Thom calculation, Künneth,
localization, and proper base change.

Edge cases: n=0, empty B, ramified E with A not flat over Z/ℓ^N. Steps 1, 2 and 4–8 are correct: the mate normalization and full faithfulness, divisor-class restriction and excision, the localization long exact sequence (H^{2n-1}=0 and the top-degree isomorphism), Kummer naturality over Ω without finite type, the clause-3 stalk detector, and exchange-forget for the A-linear mate. The DFS from the item finds no cycle. Two repairable faults were fixed. (1) C1/E5 in step 3: the step treated the internal supported cup ∂κ(t_1)∪…∪∂κ(t_n) (def-pur-supported-cup, pro-étale) as if it were the supported exterior product κ^{Z,W} that the compact lemma speaks about. No DAG node identifies the two. I added an even-degree twisted cup clause to the delivery's own new lemma lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility: κ^{Z,W}(α⊗β)=pr^*α∪pr^*β. I rewrote step 3 to use it with lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality and u_{0}=τ_E (1708 characters). (2) The same lemma defined u_Z only on cohomology classes but asserted a derived equation. u_Z is now defined in D(A) via C_i⊣RΓ_Z and RΓ_c(ε_i), with Z proper so that j_!i_*=ī_*. The excision extension is now made precise. Small: step 5 now cites def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed for RΓ(P^n,j_!A)=RΓ_c(U,A). The geometry lemma is true clause by clause and is not a duplicate of the nagata Proj/base-change nodes. Neither new node is a duplicate or restates a clause of the item. Every proof dependency is on the transitive unit route, so the declared tool_uses are unnecessary but harmless; I accept them.
